channel.title: Ebola Tracker — the letter
channel.description: Every situation report on the Ebola outbreak in the DRC, summarised on the day it is published: national figures and what the letter takes from it.

item.title: The letter no. 130 — 21 Sep 2026
item.description:
Confirmed cases : 7,773 · Deaths : 3,759 · Case fatality rate : 48.4%

In Ituri, six treatment centres remain full on the suspected-case side, the Avakubi control point still cannot open for lack of security, and only 9 zones out of 28 report their data. In Nord-Kivu, 34% of patients are treated outside the planned facilities, no bed is free in Butembo or Katwa, a control point was vandalised at Mususa, and field teams have gone unpaid for more than four months. In Tshopo, fewer than a third of the targeted health workers are vaccinated and 226 thawed doses expire on 24 September; the incinerator at the Makiso-Kisangani hospital is still out of order. In Bas-Uélé, still no treatment centre and no ambulance, and roads that cannot be used.

item.title: The letter no. 129 — 20 Sep 2026
item.description:
Confirmed cases : 7,733 · Deaths : 3,732 · Case fatality rate : 48.3%

In Ituri, six treatment centres remain full on the suspected-case side, the Avakubi control point still cannot open for lack of security, and only 10 zones out of 28 report their data. In Nord-Kivu, 34% of patients are treated outside the planned facilities, no bed is free in Butembo or Katwa, and a rumour blames the vaccine for children's deaths; in Lubero, four refusals of contact listing or decontamination, only one settled. In Tshopo, two patients who escaped the treatment centre have stayed at home and ten of their contacts refuse follow-up; 352 thawed doses expire on 24 September. In Bas-Uélé, still no treatment centre and no ambulance, and roads that cannot be used.

item.title: The letter no. 128 — 19 Sep 2026
item.description:
Confirmed cases : 7,672 · Deaths : 3,699 · Case fatality rate : 48.2%

In Ituri, six treatment centres remain full on the suspected-case side, the Avakubi control point still cannot open for lack of security, and only 13 zones out of 28 report their data. In Nord-Kivu, 42% of patients are treated outside the planned facilities, no bed is free in Butembo or Katwa, and five zones still have no decontamination team. In Tshopo, fewer than a third of the targeted health workers are vaccinated — 11% in Lubunga — and 424 thawed doses expire on 24 September; the incinerator at the Makiso-Kisangani hospital is still out of order. In Bas-Uélé, still no treatment centre and no ambulance, and roads that cannot be used.

item.title: The letter no. 127 — 18 Sep 2026
item.description:
Confirmed cases : 7,614 · Deaths : 3,676 · Case fatality rate : 48.3%

In Ituri, six treatment centres remain full on the suspected-case side, the Avakubi control point still cannot open for lack of security, and 8 zones out of 28 report their data. In Nord-Kivu, 42.9% of patients are treated outside the planned facilities, no bed is free in Butembo or Katwa, and 5 homes out of 15 have been disinfected. In Tshopo, fewer than a third of the targeted health workers are vaccinated and 631 thawed doses expire on 24 September. In Haut-Uélé, families are refusing to let bodies be tested and teams have been threatened in Isiro. In Bas-Uélé, still no treatment centre and no ambulance. In Sud-Kivu, no isolation room at any of the three entry points.

item.title: The letter no. 126 — 17 Sep 2026
item.description:
Confirmed cases : 7,541 · Deaths : 3,639 · Case fatality rate : 48.3%

In Ituri, six treatment centres are full on the suspected-case side, insecurity still prevents the Avakubi control point from opening, and only 8 zones out of 28 report their data. In Nord-Kivu, 46.2% of patients are treated outside the planned facilities, no bed is left in Butembo or Katwa, 11 homes out of 49 have been disinfected and a hygiene worker has been threatened. In Tshopo, the patient who fled the treatment centre is still at home, safe blood is lacking, and of five refusals reported only two have been resolved. In Bas-Uélé, still no treatment centre and no ambulance, and more vaccine doses are needed. In Haut-Uélé, the psychosocial teams cannot travel to Wamba or Boma Mangbetu. In Sud-Kivu, no isolation room at any of the three entry points.

item.title: The letter no. 125 — 16 Sep 2026
item.description:
Confirmed cases : 7,475 · Deaths : 3,605 · Case fatality rate : 48.2%

In Ituri, six treatment centres remain full on the suspected-case side, data reporting is weak in several zones and responders are demoralised by unpaid wages. In Nord-Kivu, 42% of patients are treated outside the planned facilities, no bed is left in Butembo or Katwa, 11 homes out of 36 have been disinfected, and community relays in Vunyakondomi are being threatened. In Tshopo, a patient who fled the centre is still at home, two cases refuse any public-health measure, and the vaccination sessions of 16 September did not take place for lack of transport. In Haut-Uélé, no communication material is left. In Bas-Uélé, still no treatment centre and no ambulance, and 16 control points active out of 41.

item.title: The letter no. 124 — 15 Sep 2026
item.description:
Confirmed cases : 7,404 · Deaths : 3,577 · Case fatality rate : 48.3%

In Ituri, 26 prevention rings out of 42 are open, ten bodies could not be tested in Fataki and Mandima, for lack of means or because families refused, and resistance is reported in Rwampara. In Nord-Kivu, 42% of patients are treated outside the planned facilities, no bed is left in Butembo or Katwa, and five zones still have no disinfection. In Tshopo, the patient who fled the centre is still at home and the incinerator is still broken. In Haut-Uélé, four control points did not report for lack of connection. In Bas-Uélé, 14 control points out of 41 are working, without trained staff, and there is no treatment centre and no ambulance.

item.title: The letter no. 123 — 14 Sep 2026
item.description:
Confirmed cases : 7,345 · Deaths : 3,545 · Case fatality rate : 48.3%

In Ituri, six treatment centres remain full on the suspected-case side, only 21 prevention rings out of 57 are open and the disinfection teams in Nizi are on strike over unpaid wages. In Nord-Kivu, 45% of patients are treated outside a centre, no bed is left in Butembo or Katwa, and five zones have no active disinfection team. In Tshopo, 18 control posts out of 30 are active, the patient who fled the centre is still at home and the incinerator is still broken. In Haut-Uélé, no communication material is left. In Bas-Uélé, still no treatment centre and no ambulance, and health workers in the five priority zones are not trained in infection prevention.

item.title: The letter no. 122 — 13 Sep 2026
item.description:
Confirmed cases : 7,258 · Deaths : 3,510 · Case fatality rate : 48.4%

In Ituri, six treatment centres remain full on the suspected-case side, 25 prevention rings out of 61 are open, nine bodies could not be tested, for lack of means in Mandima and because families refused elsewhere, and three control posts are on strike over unpaid wages. In Nord-Kivu, contact follow-up has fallen sharply, 11 homes out of 49 have been disinfected, 45% of patients are treated outside a centre, no bed is left in Butembo or Katwa, and the police guarding health facilities are unpaid. In Tshopo, a rumour of a 300-dollar bonus for every alert circulated, the patient who fled the centre is still at home and the incinerator is still broken. In Haut-Uélé, no communication material is left. In Bas-Uélé, still no treatment centre and no ambulance.

item.title: The letter no. 121 — 12 Sep 2026
item.description:
Confirmed cases : 7,200 · Deaths : 3,475 · Case fatality rate : 48.3%

In Ituri, six treatment centres remain full on the suspected-case side, 28 prevention rings out of 66 are open, families refuse safe burials in Nizi, Bambu, Komanda, Mambasa and Rwampara, and the Nzebi control post is on strike over unpaid wages. Contact follow-up is slipping in Haut-Uélé, where five control posts did not report for lack of network. In Nord-Kivu, the centres are overflowing (150% occupancy), 10 homes out of 66 have been disinfected, communication teams have gone unpaid for more than three months and community incidents, sometimes violent, are reported. In Tshopo, a community health worker was threatened for reporting a death, the patient who fled the centre is still at home and the incinerator is still broken. In Bas-Uélé, still no treatment centre and no ambulance, and the Ervebo vaccine is out of stock in Buta.

item.title: The letter no. 120 — 11 Sep 2026
item.description:
Confirmed cases : 7,113 · Deaths : 3,437 · Case fatality rate : 48.3%

In Ituri, six treatment centres remain full on the suspected-case side, 26 prevention rings out of 71 are open, the staff of three control posts are on strike over unpaid wages and insecurity still blocks the Avakubi post. Contact follow-up is slipping in Tshopo. In Nord-Kivu, the centres are overflowing (139% occupancy), nearly one patient in two is treated outside a CTE and 10 homes out of 13 have been disinfected. In Tshopo, a confirmed patient who fled the centre is still at home, the Makiso-Kisangani incinerator is still broken and the Bafwasende vaccination site is not open. In Haut-Uélé, no communication material is left, and psychosocial staff are unpaid. In Bas-Uélé, still no treatment centre and no ambulance, and the Ervebo vaccine is out of stock in Buta.

item.title: The letter no. 119 — 10 Sep 2026
item.description:
Confirmed cases : 7,022 · Deaths : 3,398 · Case fatality rate : 48.4%

In Ituri, six treatment centres remain full on the suspected-case side, 25 prevention rings out of 83 are open, 14 bodies could not be tested for lack of means, refusals of safe burial persist in four zones and the staff of five control posts are on strike over unpaid wages. Contact follow-up is below the threshold in 3 provinces out of 5. In Nord-Kivu, 10 homes out of 27 have been disinfected and teams still need training in five zones. In Tshopo, a confirmed patient who fled the treatment centre is still at home, the Makiso-Kisangani incinerator is broken and vaccination received only 4,500 doses out of 11,000 requested. In Haut-Uélé, communication staff have not been paid for two months. In Bas-Uélé, still no treatment centre or ambulance, and the Ervebo vaccine is lacking in Buta.

item.title: The letter no. 118 — 9 Sep 2026
item.description:
Confirmed cases : 6,942 · Deaths : 3,349 · Case fatality rate : 48.2%

In Ituri, the treatment centres of Nizi, Mambasa, Lolwa, Kilo, Mangala and Mandima remain full on the suspected-case side and 30 patients are in critical condition; 24 prevention rings were opened out of 77 expected, disinfection teams are lacking in Mangala and Komanda, transport in Bambu, Mandima and Mangala, supplies in Mandima, and refusals of safe burial are reported in Bunia, Nizi, Nia-Nia and Aru; the Avakubi control point remains closed because of insecurity and the staff of four posts (Nzebi, Galay, Base Yedi and Marabo) are still on strike over unpaid wages; only 13 health zones out of 36 know the mechanism for reporting sexual abuse. Contact follow-up is below the threshold in 4 provinces out of 5. In Nord-Kivu, disinfection teams still need to be activated and trained in Biena, Masereka, Kyondo, Mabalako and Vuhovi, some homes due for disinfection cannot be traced and the teams lack vehicles; a confirmed patient fled in Masereka and a family in Munzambaye, in the Butembo zone, refuses the disinfection of its home; the security team has no permanent vehicle; psychosocial support does not reach the latest cases in nine zones and 10 zones have no crèche. In Tshopo, teams were attacked in Bethsaïda, in the Mangobo zone, amid rumours of “Ebola business”, 11 contacts refuse follow-up in Matete, safe blood is lacking, the incinerator of the Makiso-Kisangani hospital is still broken, vaccination received only 4,500 doses out of 11,000 requested and the Bafwasende site is not open. In Haut-Uélé, the Pawa centre lacks hygiene facilities and the Isiro centre lacks space, water and electricity; 4 control posts out of 11 have no internet; in Tely, a family still refuses to be counted, and a rumour that patients are locked up under the tents of the Isiro hospital is circulating. In Sud-Kivu, 5 control posts out of 9 reported. In Bas-Uélé, still no treatment centre or ambulance, no report from the control posts, and the Ervebo vaccine shortage in Buta suspends vaccination.

item.title: The letter no. 117 — 8 Sep 2026
item.description:
Confirmed cases : 6,843 · Deaths : 3,310 · Case fatality rate : 48.4%

In Ituri, the treatment centres of Nizi, Mambasa, Lolwa, Kilo, Mangala and Mandima are full on the suspected-case side and 30 patients are in critical condition; 15 prevention rings were opened out of 59 expected, disinfection teams are lacking in Fataki, Mangala and Komanda, transport in Bambu and Mandima, supplies in Mangala and Mandima, and refusals of safe burial are reported in Bunia, Nizi, Nia-Nia and Aru; the Avakubi control point remains closed because of insecurity. In Nord-Kivu, 13 homes were disinfected out of 47 identified, teams still need training in Biena, Masereka, Kyondo, Mabalako and Vuhovi, a confirmed patient fled in Masereka and a family in Munzambaye, in the Butembo zone, refuses the disinfection of its home. In Tshopo, teams were attacked in Bethsaïda, in the Mangobo zone, amid rumours of “Ebola business”, 11 contacts refuse follow-up in Matete, safe blood is lacking, the incinerator of the Makiso-Kisangani hospital is broken, vaccination received only 3,000 doses out of 11,000 requested, and 18 control posts out of 30 are active. In Haut-Uélé, the Pawa centre lacks hygiene facilities and the Isiro centre lacks space, water and electricity; in Tely, a family still refuses to be counted, and a rumour says patients are locked up under the tents of the Isiro hospital. In Bas-Uélé, still no treatment centre or ambulance, too few teams to follow contacts, and the Ervebo vaccine remains out of stock in Buta.

item.title: The letter no. 116 — 7 Sep 2026
item.description:
Confirmed cases : 6,757 · Deaths : 3,267 · Case fatality rate : 48.3%

In Nord-Kivu, 101 of the 254 hospitalised patients, or 40%, are treated in facilities that are not treatment centres; in Masereka, a confirmed patient fled after his result was announced, and a family in Munzambaye, in the Butembo zone, refuses the disinfection of its home. In Ituri, the centres of Nizi, Mambasa, Lolwa and Kilo are full on the suspected-case side, 25 prevention rings were opened out of 70 expected, bodies could not be tested in Mandima and Fataki for lack of teams, and refusals of safe burial are reported in Bunia, Nizi, Nia-Nia and Aru; in Nord-Kivu, 8 bodies were not tested in Kalunguta and Vuhovi for lack of transport. In Tshopo, teams were attacked in Bethsaïda, in the Mangobo zone, amid rumours of “Ebola business”, 11 contacts refuse follow-up in Matete, safe blood is lacking, and vaccination received only 3,000 doses out of 11,000 requested. In Haut-Uélé, the Pawa centre lacks hygiene facilities and the Isiro centre lacks space, water and electricity; a rumour says patients are locked up under the tents of the Isiro hospital. In Bas-Uélé, still no treatment centre or ambulance, too few teams to follow contacts, and the Ervebo vaccine remains out of stock in Buta. At control points, four posts in Ituri are on strike for lack of pay, Avakubi remains closed because of insecurity, and Tshopo has activated only 18 posts out of 30.

item.title: The letter no. 115 — 6 Sep 2026
item.description:
Confirmed cases : 6,686 · Deaths : 3,226 · Case fatality rate : 48.3%

In Nord-Kivu, treatment centres are at 123% of their capacity and patients are still treated in facilities not meant for Ebola. In Ituri, the centres of Nizi, Mambasa and Mandima are full on the suspected-case side, 39 patients are in critical condition, and prevention is falling behind: 15 prevention rings opened out of 69 expected, 5 bodies that could not be tested in Nia-Nia and Mandima because families objected, and too few disinfection teams in Fataki, Mangala and Komanda. At control points, four posts in Ituri (Nzebi, Galay, Pluto and Bey) are on strike for lack of pay, the Avakubi post remains closed because of insecurity, and Tshopo has activated only 18 of its 30 planned posts. In Haut-Uélé, a confirmed patient who had fled was found in Nduka and refuses to return to the treatment centre; 22 contacts were listed along her route. In Tshopo, 10 contacts refuse follow-up in Matete. In Bas-Uélé, everything is missing at once: teams to follow contacts, a treatment centre, an ambulance, and the Ervebo vaccine, out of stock in Buta, which suspends the vaccination of health workers. Control-point reports arrive at only 34.6% in Bas-Uélé, 55.5% in Sud-Kivu and 64.0% in Haut-Uélé.

item.title: The letter no. 114 — 5 Sep 2026
item.description:
Confirmed cases : 6,604 · Deaths : 3,175 · Case fatality rate : 48.1%

In Nord-Kivu, treatment centres are overflowing, at 115% of their capacity, and patients are treated in facilities not meant for Ebola; in Beni, residents are threatening to burn down the Ndindi morgue after the body of a confirmed patient was taken away. In Ituri, prevention lags behind: 18 prevention rings set up out of 60 expected around new cases, 30 bodies that could not be tested because families objected, 19 patients who refused to be hospitalised in a single day, and 2,581 travellers who refused the temperature check at control points, plus 228 in Haut-Uélé, because of rumours of poisoned water and thermometers. In Bas-Uélé, everything is missing at once: teams to follow contacts, a treatment centre, an ambulance, and the Ervebo vaccine, out of stock, which interrupts the vaccination of health workers. Two response teams did not send their figures: the control points of Bas-Uélé, and Sud-Kivu, where only 55% of the expected reports arrived.

item.title: The letter no. 113 — 4 Sep 2026
item.description:
Confirmed cases : 6,522 · Deaths : 3,134 · Case fatality rate : 48.1%

In Ituri, prevention rings are set up around only 29% of new cases (12 of 41), teams are lacking in Fataki, Mangala and Nizi; 21 patients refused to be hospitalised, 7 bodies could not be tested because families objected; the treatment centre of the CME hospital in Bunia is full for confirmed patients, those of Nizi, Lita, Mambasa and Logo for suspected patients, and the extension of Nizi and Bambu is delayed. In Nord-Kivu, patients are treated in facilities not meant for Ebola; a confirmed patient ran away in Katwa, another in Lubero refuses to go to the transit centre, and residents threaten to burn the centre under construction in Katwa. In Bas-Uélé, no prevention ring set up, neither a centre up to standard nor an ambulance, the waste-treatment area of the Buta hospital does not work, the Ganga and Viadana hospitals do not sort patients at the entrance, vaccination teams have no vehicle and six zones have no plan to vaccinate health workers; control points did not send their figures. In Tshopo, residents' opposition and untraceable addresses prevent prevention rings around the last three patients, blood for transfusions is still lacking, 12 of 30 control points are working and three zones have no psychological support worker. Contact follow-up lacks teams.

item.title: The letter no. 112 — 3 Sep 2026
item.description:
Confirmed cases : 6,436 · Deaths : 3,095 · Case fatality rate : 48.1%

In Nord-Kivu, centres hold 102.7% of their capacity and more than half of patients, 51.7%, are treated in facilities not meant for Ebola; a family in Katsya (Butembo) hesitates to let its home be disinfected and the Kalunguta team was assaulted in Mataba. In Ituri, prevention rings are set up around three new cases in four (20 of 27); 21 patients refused to be hospitalised in Rwampara, Bunia, Tchomia and Lolwa, 9 bodies could not be tested in Bambu, Fataki and Mandima; the Lita centre is full and the extension of Nizi and Bambu is delayed; four control points are on strike. In Tshopo, residents prevent the prevention ring around the 20th patient, blood for transfusions has been lacking for six days, only one health facility out of 79 follows hygiene rules at more than 80%, and 18 of 30 control points are working. In Bas-Uélé, no prevention ring set up, six zones whose health workers are not trained in hygiene, two hospitals without sorting of patients at the entrance, neither a centre up to standard nor an ambulance. In Haut-Uélé, 209 travellers refused the temperature check at Magambe, 19 recovered people left Isiro without a home-return kit, and vaccination teams have no vehicle.

item.title: The letter no. 111 — 2 Sep 2026
item.description:
Confirmed cases : 6,342 · Deaths : 3,072 · Case fatality rate : 48.4%

In Ituri, prevention rings are set up around one new case in three (18 of 55); 21 patients refused to be hospitalised, 11 bodies could not be tested because families objected, and residents resist in Rwampara, Nyankunde, Bunia, Tchomia, Lita, Mangala and Kilo; the Nizi centre is full and eight control points are closed by a strike of unpaid staff. In Nord-Kivu, centres hold 118.6% of their capacity and patients are treated in facilities not meant for Ebola; 14 homes disinfected out of 35. In Bas-Uélé, no prevention ring set up, no home disinfected, five zones whose health workers are not trained in hygiene, neither a treatment centre up to standard nor an ambulance, and control points lack vehicles, connectivity and water. In Haut-Uélé, four control points did not send their figures and 12% of travellers refuse hand-washing at Magambe. In Tshopo, no centre up to standard in Bafwasende, no blood bags left for transfusions, and residents still oppose investigations and transfers.
